 THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER

The petitioners-accused Nos.1 and 3 are before this Court seeking grant of anticipatory bail in Crime No.11/2024 of Vyalika Police Station, pending on the file of the learned III Additional CMM Court,
Bengaluru, registered for the offences punishable under Sections 120B, 418, 409, 419, 420, 467,
468, 417 read with Section 34 of Indian Penal Code (for short 'IPC'), on the basis of the first information lodged by the informant- Sri.Parthasarathi.
2. Heard Sri.Narayanaswamy K.N., learned counsel for the petitioners and Sri.Rahul Rai K., learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent-State.
Perused the materials on record.

3. In view of the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel for both the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is:
NC: 2024:KHC:20597 "Whether the petitioners are entitled for grant of bail under Section 438 of Cr.P.C.?"

My answer to the above point is in 'Partly in Affirmative' for the following:
REASONS 4.
The petitioners arrayed as accused Nos.1 and 3 are seeking grant of anticipatory bail on apprehension of being arrested.

The Regional Head of Central Bank of India, R.M.V.Extension Branch, Bengaluru lodged the first information against accused Nos.1 to 3 making serious allegations and invoking the penal provisions as stated above.
It is stated that accused No.1 approached the branch seeking loan under MUDRA Scheme.
Accordingly, loan of Rs.90.00 lakhs was sanctioned.
Earlier, loan of Rs.10.00 lakhs was sanctioned.
Totally, an amount of Rs.1 crore was disbursed to the account furnished by accused No.1.
It is stated that accused No.2 being the Manager gave false report with regard to the business of accused No.1.
It is stated that for the purpose of purchasing the machineries, accused Nos.1 and 2 have furnished fake address and gave false information to claim the subsidy.
No NC: 2024:KHC:20597 part of the loan obtained was repaid by accused No.1.
On enquiry with another officer of the Bank, it was found that accused Nos.1 and 2 had furnished false information and fake documents for the purpose of obtaining loan in that bank.
It is also stated that accused No.1 never undertook any business as proclaimed.
5. It is stated that accused No.2 was apprehended and subsequently he was enlarged on bail.
Whereas, accused No.1 is seeking for grant of anticipatory bail.

Looking to the nature and Smt Sumathi N vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48047489/
2 seriousness of the offence, petitioner - accused No.1 is not entitled to grant of anticipatory bail.
6.

sentences.text: Accused No.3 is the daughter of accused No.1.
No specific overt act is alleged against her.
The only allegation made against her is that, she had also accompanied accused No.1 to the Bank for furnishing the fake documents and giving false information.
Apart from that there are no other serious allegations against her.
Therefore, I am of the opinion that petitioner - accused No.3 is entitled for grant of anticipatory bail, subject to conditions, which will take care of the interest of the prosecution.

Accordingly, I answer the above point partly in the affirmative and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition against petitioner - accused No.1 is dismissed.
The petition filed by petitioner No.2-accused No.3 is allowed.

The petitioner - accused No.3 is ordered to be enlarged on bail in the event of her arrest in Crime No.11/2024 of Vyalika Police Station, pending on the file of the learned III Additional CMM Court, Bengaluru.

The petitioner - accused No.3 is directed to appear before the Investigating Officer within 15 days from the date of receipt of this order and on her appearance, the Investigating Officer shall enlarge her on bail subject to the following conditions:-
a.
The petitioner - accused No.3 shall not commit any offences;

c. The petitioner - accused No.3 shall appear before the Investigating Officer or the court as and when required; and d. The petitioner - accused No.3 shall not threaten or tamper the prosecution witnesses.
On furnishing the sureties by the petitioner - accused No.3, the Investigating Officer is at liberty to verify the correctness of the address and authenticity of the documents furnished by her.
On satisfaction of the said documents, she may proceed to accept the sureties within a reasonable time.
